title: Redwood security/BCDR incident response & SLA review - Aurora Bank
summary: Redwood walked through incident response and BCDR capabilities focused on RTO/RPO, SLA uptime targets, and the escalation process. Discussed SOC2 artifacts, KMS options (BYOK/HSM), audit log retention and regional data residency. Aurora requested tabletop exercise and SOC 2 Type II report; asked for clearer RTO/RPO commitments per deployment mode and escalation SLAs for P1 incidents.
next_steps: Samir to send SOC 2 Type II report and encryption whitepaper
Elena to share BCDR runbook excerpt and sample escalation matrix
Schedule 60-min tabletop incident exercise w/ Aurora ops - target week of 2026-03-22
Provide pricing addendum for Dedicated with 99.95% SLA and optional faster RTO tier
action_items: Samir Patel - send SOC 2 Type II report and encryption whitepaper - due 2026-03-15
Elena Ruiz - export excerpt of BCDR runbook + escalation matrix - due 2026-03-16
Ben Carter (Aurora) - propose 3 candidate dates for tabletop exercise - due 2026-03-18
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Chris (Redwood CSM); Mark (Aurora Head of Security), Aisha (Aurora Ops), Ben (Platform Eng), Priya (Compliance)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm Samir from Redwood, i'll kick us off. quick agenda: incident response, rto/rpo expectations, sla uptimes, and how our escalation process works. elena will walk through the runbook.
[00:22] Mark: great, thanks. just to set context, aurora is evaluating you for core inference on sensitive customer PII workloads. our compliance team is real picky about rto, rpo, key management and audit trails.
[00:35] Elena: totally, we'll go through SOC 2 artifacts, KMS options including BYOK and hsm integrations, and the exact escalation flow for p1s. quick note: transcription might show "Redwood Dedicate" sometimes, we actually mean Redwood Dedicated.
[00:50] Aisha: cool, our baseline questions — what are the promised rto/rpo numbers for hosted vs dedicated vs private? and who owns failover orchestration?
[01:05] Elena: good question. high level: Hosted (shared) — standard plan: we commit 99.9% monthly uptime; typical rto around 4 hours and rpo up to 1 hour for customer-facing state. Dedicated — with reserved capacity we target 99.95% uptime, and for the dedicated enterprise tier we can offer rto ~1 hour and rpo 15 minutes with cross-region replication and automated failover. Private / on-prem — rto/rpo depend on customer setup; we provide runbooks and orchestration hooks and can support tighter sla in the contract.
[01:40] Mark: rpo 15 minutes on dedicated — is that dependent on a feature toggle? does that require enabling continuous cross-region replication?
[01:50] Elena: yes it's tied to the replication policy. we do continuous async replication of model state/prefix caches and job metadata. for KV cache we persist snapshots every X minutes — i should attach the exact doc. there are tradeoffs vs cost, which the optimize team can model.
[02:10] Ben: how do you handle in-flight requests during failover? i.e., if a region fails mid-request are tokens lost or reprocessed?
[02:20] Elena: there can be partial replays; for idempotent calls we recommend request ids and retry logic. our runtime keeps ephemeral kvs per session but we replicate job metadata so you can rehydrate sessions; not all ephemeral caches survive an immediate failover. we'll include recommended client retry patterns.
[02:45] Priya: SOC 2 — do you have Type II and do you provide the report under NDA? also do you have iso 27001?
[02:55] Samir: we have SOC 2 Type II, and we will share the report under NDA. we are ISO-pending (in progress) — i'll confirm the iso status and include dates.
[03:10] Mark: audit logs retention — we need 1 year of admin audit logs and 7 years for certain compliance artifacts. does Redwood store detailed admin actions?
[03:20] Chris: yes, our console emits audit logs for admin actions, api keys, role changes, and model deployments. retention default is 90 days but we have longer retention add-ons; we'll map the log types to retention buckets in the doc.
[03:40] Aisha: encryption — does Redwood support bring-your-own-key (byok)? do you do envelope encryption and can keys be in customer hsm / ksm?
[03:52] Elena: we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private modes. hosted customers can use cloud-kms integration or opt for a managed key; we support envelope encryption with keys wrapping via customer kms. for full hsm-backed keys we partner with cloud hsm providers; i'll attach the architecture diagram.
[04:10] Ben: key rotation and access controls — can we rotate without downtime? how are keys audited?
[04:18] Elena: rotation is supported and can be staged; typical pattern is new key wraps new envelopes while old envelopes remain decryptable; there is no platform-wide downtime. all kms operations are logged to audit trail and we provide key usage logs in the audit export.
[04:35] Mark: escalation process — for p1 incidents what is the contact path? pager? phone? sla times for acknowledging?
[04:45] Samir: standard p1 is acknowledged by on-call within 15 minutes, with targeted remediation update every 30 minutes until recovery. escalation matrix: tier 1 eng on-call -> se/tier 2 -> engineering manager -> director of platform -> exec on-call. for enterprise we can codify alternative contacts and escalation steps in the contract.
[05:10] Priya: are there guaranteed response times in the sla or just best-effort?
[05:15] Samir: for Dedicated enterprise customers we put response windows in the sla: p1 ack < 15 mins, p2 < 60 mins. credits apply if we miss uptime targets, and there is a formal claim process. i'll share the sla pdf.
[05:35] Aisha: do you run tabletop exercises with customers? we want to simulate a region outage and see the failover.
[05:42] Elena: yes, we do. we recommend a 60-min tabletop with ops and security to walk through detection, escalation, and failover playbook. we'll help run it and provide artifacts.
[05:55] Ben: what about incident forensics — you mentioned retention tiers. if we need packet logs or deeper telemetry for an incident how long does that exist and at what cost?
[06:06] Chris: detailed telemetry is available but typically short-lived due to volume; we can export to your SIEM for long-term retention. we also produce incident reports with timelines, root cause analysis, and remediation steps.
[06:25] Speaker 1: (background) is there a demo of the runbook?
[06:28] Elena: i'll share a sanitized excerpt of our BCDR runbook; it has step-by-step checklist, signal thresholds, playbooks for network partition, node failure, and region failover. it'll include who to call per step.
[06:40] Mark: data residency — our customers in eu require data not to cross regions. how do you guarantee region residency for logs and keys?
[06:51] Elena: we can pin customers to a region for compute and storage. for hosted deployments we have region-specific clusters; audit logs and cold backups can be scoped to region. keys can be stored in region-specific kms. we'll detail the data flows in the doc.
[07:10] Aisha: SLA credit examples — can you summarize how credits are calculated? we've seen wild variations.
[07:18] Samir: typical formula is pro-rated based on downtime minutes vs monthly uptime; example: 99.95% allows ~22 minutes downtime/month. credits tiers escalate with lower uptime. details in the sla pdf i'll share.
[07:35] Ben: on the technical deep dive side, how does your runtime do graceful degradation? e.g., if capacity is tight do you auto-fail to a lower-cost model or queue requests?
[07:47] Elena: we have routing policies: latency-priority will reject or queue when overloaded; cost-priority can route to quantized variants; and we have fallbacks to cached responses for repeat prompts. those are per-route configs. for BCDR we prefer explicit failover to avoid silent degradation.
[08:05] Priya: incident evidence — do you provide signed timeline logs for compliance audits?
[08:12] Chris: we can provide verified incident timelines and supporting logs. where necessary we do redacted exports to protect PII.
[08:25] Mark: ok, a few concrete asks: 1) SOC2 Type II under nda 2) a BCDR runbook excerpt 3) SLA doc with credit examples and p1/p2 times 4) escalation matrix contact list; 5) propose tabletop dates.
[08:40] Samir: noted. we'll deliver items 1-4 by next week and propose tabletop dates.
[08:48] Aisha: one more — backups and rpo for model artifacts and finetune snapshots. if we lose a model version do you keep artifacts long term?
[08:57] Elena: model artifacts are stored in blob storage with snapshots; default snapshot cadence is daily with a 30-day retention, can be extended for enterprise. we replicate artifacts cross-region for dedicated tiers — that supports the 15-min rpo claim for metadata; model weights are large so we replicate on a schedule and snapshot frequently to minimize loss.
[09:20] Ben: is there a runbook for data corruption scenarios?
[09:25] Elena: yes, we have checksums and integrity checks, and a corruption playbook that rolls back to last known-good snapshot; we can run quarantines and forensic analysis.
[09:40] Mark: how about legal / subpoena handling and logs for audit — do you have formal processes?
[09:47] Chris: we have a legal process; subpoenas are handled via our legal team and we produce logs under legal compulsion. we'll share the process docs with redactions for privacy.
[10:00] Priya: can we get an example escalation contact with phone number and pager? we need to provision our internal contacts to align with yours.
[10:07] Samir: we'll provide an example escalation matrix with phone/pager/email placeholders; for production you'll later provide your on-call roster so we can lock that into the contract.
[10:20] Aisha: couple of edge cases: 1) what if the private control plane can't reach on-prem nodes (air gap) — how do you help troubleshoot?
[10:30] Elena: in air-gapped cases we provide an ops bundle — local runbook, support agent access via jumpbox, and offline toolkits; for full private deployments we offer an optional on-site support package.
[10:45] Mark: tabletop exercise logistics — will you run blameless postmortems? we require that to be part of the exercise.
[10:52] Chris: yes, we run blameless postmortems and produce a PDF w/ root cause analysis, timeline, and action items.
[11:00] Ben: can you send sample runbook snippets showing alert thresholds?
[11:05] Elena: yes i'll attach snippets. sample thresholds: 5xx rate >1% for 3 mins triggers p1; sustained queue backlog > 500 requests triggers p2; region packet loss >30% triggers failover. these are example thresholds we tune with customers.
[11:28] Priya: last question — are audit logs tamper-evident? can we demonstrate chain-of-custody?
[11:35] Chris: logs are append-only in our storage and we can provide digests/hashes to demonstrate tamper evidence; for stronger chain-of-custody we recommend exporting to your own log store or using signed exports.
[11:50] Samir: ok let's recap next steps and owners. elena will share the runbook excerpt and escalation matrix. i'll send SOC 2 and sla pdf. chris will coordinate tabletop scheduling. ben will propose dates.
[12:05] Mark: sounds good. thanks everyone. we'll review the docs and come back with any follow-ups.
[12:12] Samir: thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
